mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1.5% relative to its 12-month average compresses discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.0% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth falls below 0.5% year-over-year, the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to combined monetary tightening and labor market weakness.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.5% YoY) occurs in > 50% of cases but 20-day returns are positive in > 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate slower economic growth and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in monetary tightening cycles are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the cycle duration is less than 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.1 million units signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1.1 million occurs in > 30% of cases but 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is declining year-over-year and GDP growth (GDPC1) is below 1.5%, the S&P 500 experiences negative 60-day forward returns due to a contraction in the real economy.
failure_condition: The joint condition (INDPRO YoY decline and GDPC1 growth < 1.5%) occurs in > 40% of cases but 60-day returns are positive in > 45% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong nonfarm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% year-over-year consistently predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as it signals a robust labor market and strong consumer spending.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in strong payroll periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the Federal Reserve may accelerate rate hikes.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY occurs in > 25% of cases but 5-day returns are positive in > 55% of those instances.
